questions.q: How is a backdoor (trojan) attack conceptually structured, according to this lesson?
options: A model is trained to fail on every single input, regardless of content
A model behaves normally on ordinary inputs but produces a chosen output whenever a specific trigger pattern is present
A model refuses to produce any output unless given administrator credentials
A model only misbehaves when its weights are quantized to a lower precision
questions.explain: A backdoor acts like a hidden switch: normal behavior everywhere, except a specific, attacker-chosen output whenever a particular trigger pattern appears in the input.

questions.q: Why does a standard held-out accuracy test typically fail to catch a backdoored model?
options: Held-out test sets are always generated by the attacker
Accuracy tests only work on models smaller than 1 million parameters
The held-out test set almost certainly doesn't happen to contain the attacker's specific trigger
Backdoored models always have lower accuracy on every input, making them obvious
questions.explain: Because a backdoored model performs normally on anything that doesn't contain its specific trigger, and a test set is unlikely to contain that exact trigger by chance, standard evaluation misses it.

questions.q: What does STRIP (STRong Intentional Perturbation) check for at inference time?
options: Whether the model's prediction confidence stays suspiciously stable when random patterns are superimposed on an input
Whether the model's file size matches its published checksum
Whether the training dataset contains duplicate rows
Whether the model was trained using pickle or safetensors
questions.explain: STRIP superimposes random perturbations and watches for abnormally stable, confident predictions — a sign the trigger, not the rest of the input, is driving the output.

questions.q: How does Neural Cleanse detect a likely backdoored output class?
options: By checking the publisher's reputation on a model hub
By comparing the model's file hash against a known-good registry
By retraining the entire model from scratch with clean data
By searching for the smallest input perturbation that flips a prediction into that class, and flagging abnormally small, consistent ones
questions.explain: Neural Cleanse searches each class for the minimal perturbation that triggers misclassification into it; a legitimate class needs a large change, while a backdoored class needs an abnormally small, consistent one.

questions.q: What does activation clustering examine to detect poisoned training examples?
options: The file format the dataset is stored in
The publisher's download count on a model hub
Internal neuron activation patterns, looking for a small anomalous cluster within a labeled class
The number of GPUs used during training
questions.explain: Activation clustering looks at how training examples activate a model's internal neurons, searching for a small, statistically unusual cluster within a class that behaves differently from the rest.
